title: Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations
question: What system addresses the cross-database I/O latency and noise problems of heterogeneous vector and graph memory stores for long-term conversational agents, and what are its three core components?
gold_answer: Mandol is an agglomerative memory system that unifies memory representation and storage into a single memory-native architecture. Its three core components are a hierarchical memory model (basic and abstract layers as structured semantic graphs), an agglomerative semantic data structure combining SemanticMap and SemanticGraph for unified hybrid retrieval, and a quantitative query mechanism with query-adaptive routing, denoising, conflict resolution, and token-constrained context generation.
supporting_quote: We propose Mandol, an agglomerative memory system that consolidates fragmented memory representations and storage into a unified memory-native architecture. Its core components include: (1) a hierarchical memory model that organizes memory into a basic layer representing raw memory information and a high-level abstract layer that agglomerates basic memories into traceable abstract memories, both uniformly represented as structured semantic graphs; (2) an agglomerative semantic data structure combining SemanticMap and SemanticGraph, which natively fuses key-value, vector, and graph structures and provides unified hybrid retrieval operators to eliminate cross-database I/O; and (3) a quantitative query mechanism with query-adaptive routing, quantitative denoising and conflict resolution, and token-constrained context generation, all without involving LLMs during retrieval

title: Mandol: An Agglomerative Agent Memory System for Long-Term Conversations
question: In an agentic memory system's denoising step, what statistical measure is used to set a dynamic score threshold that robustly filters low-scoring noisy retrieval candidates without assuming a normal score distribution?
gold_answer: A dynamic threshold based on the median absolute deviation (MAD), computed as the median relevance score minus a scaling factor kappa times the MAD of the scores.
supporting_quote: we apply a dynamic threshold based on the median absolute deviation (MAD), which robustly filters low-scoring noisy candidates without assuming normality

title: An introduction to reservoir computing
question: What machine learning demonstration used a physical container of water as the computational reservoir, and how was input provided to it?
gold_answer: A bucket of water was used as a reservoir computing system for classification tasks; input data was mechanically fed into the bucket and recordings of the resulting water surface were used for classification.
supporting_quote: You know that it is possible to perform machine learning tasks on a computer, but did you know that it is also possible to do so with a bucket of water? Precisely that was demonstrated in Ref. [12]. Input data was mechanically fed into a bucket, recordings of the water surface then could be used for classification tasks.

title: An introduction to reservoir computing
question: In an approach to energy-efficient computing that exploits Brownian motion of magnetic skyrmions, what advantage was experimentally demonstrated for this reservoir computing scheme?
gold_answer: Brownian reservoir computing based on skyrmions was realized experimentally and shown to be very promising for energy-efficient computing, since it exploits thermal fluctuations that are already present in the system.
supporting_quote: Brownian RC based on skyrmions was realized experimentally by Raab et al. [41], who demonstrated that this approach is very promising for energy-efficient computing.

title: CacheRAG- A Semantic Caching System for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Knowledge Graph Question Answering
question: What system architecture addresses schema hallucination and limited retrieval coverage in LLM-driven knowledge graph question answering by caching past retrieval plans instead of generating them from scratch each time, and what are its three core design principles?
gold_answer: The system is a cache-augmented architecture (CacheRAG) for LLM-based KGQA that turns stateless planners into continual learners. Its three design principles are a schema-agnostic user interface via a two-stage semantic parsing framework with an Intermediate Semantic Representation and Backend Adapter, diversity-optimized cache retrieval using a two-layer hierarchical index with Maximal Marginal Relevance, and bounded heuristic expansion via deterministic depth/breadth subgraph operators.
supporting_quote: We propose CacheRAG, a systematic cache-augmented architecture for LLM-based KGQA that transforms stateless planners into continual learners.

title: CacheRAG- A Semantic Caching System for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Knowledge Graph Question Answering
question: In a cache-augmented KGQA retrieval system using Maximal Marginal Relevance over cached query plans, what is the default value of the MMR penalty parameter and how many structurally diverse plans are sampled for the LLM query compiler?
gold_answer: The default MMR penalty parameter λ is set to 0.5, and the sample size k of structurally diverse plans provided to the LLM Query Compiler is set to 5.
supporting_quote: The default MMR penalty parameter λ is set to 0.5. The sample size k for the struc-turally diverse plans provided to the LLM Query Compiler is set to 5.

title: Symbolic local refinement of tetrahedral grids
question: How can geometric information about tetrahedra in a local grid refinement tree be represented so that vertex locations and neighbor addresses are computed by symbolic manipulation rather than numerical computation?
gold_answer: An addressing scheme stores all geometric information about the tetrahedra as symbolic labels (expressions in an algebra of translations, permutations, rotations, and scalings), and vertex locations and nearest-neighbor addresses are found by decoding these symbols, with bisection and face-compatible refinement performed via symbolic and logical operations on the tree's leaves.
supporting_quote: An addressing scheme stores all the geometric information about the tetrahedra in the refinement tree. Location of vertices and the addresses of physically nearest neighbors are computed by decoding the symbols of the simplex address.

question: What prior bisection algorithm for local refinement of simplicial grids in n-dimensional space serves as the basis for a 3-dimensional symbolic addressing scheme?
gold_answer: Maubach's algorithm, a simple bisection algorithm for local refinement of simplicial grids in n-dimensional space that bisects a chosen edge starting from a reference simplex, is the basis extended to a 3D symbolic addressing scheme.

title: mach-batlle-magnetic-replicator

title: Local bisection refinement for $n$-simplicial grids generated by reflection
question: For a local bisection refinement algorithm on n-simplicial grids, how does the number of congruency classes produced scale with the dimension n and the level of refinement?
gold_answer: The number of congruency classes created by the bisection method is bounded above by n (in fact shown to equal n), independent of the level of refinement.
supporting_quote: Further, the number of congruency classes in a locally refined grid turns out to be bounded above by n, independent of the level of refinement.

title: Local bisection refinement for $n$-simplicial grids generated by reflection
question: What structural requirement must be satisfied by the vertex ordering of simplices in a bisection-based local grid refinement algorithm for n-simplicial grids?
gold_answer: The algorithm requires that the vertices of each simplex be ordered in a special way relative to those in neighboring simplices, with the edges to be bisected determined solely by this vertex ordering, without any local or global computation or communication.
supporting_quote: The algorithm requires that the vertices of each simplex be ordered in a special way relative to those in neighboring simplices. It is proven that certain regular simplicial grids on [0, 1]n have this property, and the more general grids to which this method is applicable are discussed. title: Recursive Algorithms for Distributed Forests of Octrees

title: Recursive Algorithms for Distributed Forests of Octrees
question: What three recursive algorithms are presented for handling topology and search in forest-of-octrees mesh data structures?
gold_answer: A parallel search for leaves matching multiple search criteria (e.g., points or polytopes), a ghost layer construction algorithm that works on arbitrarily refined octrees without requiring a 2:1 balance condition, and a universal mesh topology iterator that visits every cell and interface and computes local topological information.
supporting_quote: We present three important algorithms with recursive implementations. The first is a parallel search for leaves matching any of a set of multiple search criteria, such as leaves that contain points or intersect polytopes. The second is a ghost layer construction algorithm that handles arbitrarily refined octrees that are not covered by previous algorithms, which require a 2:1 condition between neighboring leaves. The third is a universal mesh topology iterator.

title: Fast intersections on nested tetrahedrons (FINT): An algorithm for adaptive finite element based distributed parameter estimation
question: What problem does an algorithm for handling independently refined dual tetrahedral meshes in finite-element based tomographic reconstruction solve, and how is its computational efficiency demonstrated?
gold_answer: The algorithm identifies and resolves intersections between tetrahedrons in independently refined or coarsened dual meshes, which previously had no efficient solution, enabling fully adaptive dual-mesh finite elements. Its efficiency is demonstrated via diffuse photon density wave solutions from single- and dual-mesh computations and by reconstructing a fluorescent inclusion in a simulated phantom from boundary frequency-domain fluorescence measurements.
supporting_quote: Till date, no efficient method has been reported to identify and resolve intersection between tetrahedrons in independently refined or coarsened dual meshes.

title: Fast intersections on nested tetrahedrons (FINT): An algorithm for adaptive finite element based distributed parameter estimation

gold_answer: The nested dual meshes are generated using an 8-similar subtetrahedron subdivision scheme.
supporting_quote: we report a fast and robust algorithm to identify and resolve intersection of tetrahedrons within nested dual meshes generated by 8-similar subtetrahedron subdivision scheme.

title: Open Ontologies- Tool-Augmented Ontology Engineering with Stable Matching Alignment
question: What method achieves F1 = 0.832 on the OAEI Anatomy ontology alignment track, and how does removing it affect performance?
